authentication_notes: /auth/register and /auth/verifyTelegramUser do not require authentication; all other endpoints require prior login or session token. Municipality staff registration requires admin-level auth. Telegram verification creation is tied to current user session.
Email verification and resend are public but depend on prior citizen registration.
All report management, citizen listing, and notification operations require authenticated sessions.
Operations marked auth_required need an authenticated session during test setup.
dependencies: /auth/register-municipality depends on /auth/login for session establishment. /citizens/* endpoints depend on /auth/login or /auth/register + /auth/verify-email. /reports/* (except public) depend on /auth/login. Staff management (/staffs, /offices) depends on prior staff registration via /auth/register-municipality.
/reports/{reportId}/manage and related actions depend on existence of a report created via POST /reports or POST /reports/telegram.

risks: /auth/register-municipality claims admin-only but lacks explicit role validation in schema; risk of privilege escalation if not enforced server-side. /reports/telegram endpoint requires auth_required: true despite being a bot endpoint; may cause confusion about whether Telegram bot token is passed via header or body. No operation_id fields provided, making correlation difficult for clients. Email verification and resend do not specify rate limits or expiration, risking abuse. Telegram verification flow lacks explicit link between createTelegramVerification and verifyTelegramUser (e.g., code lifetime).

Public reports endpoint (/reports/public) may expose sensitive data if filtering logic is weak. No pagination parameters documented on list endpoints, potentially causing performance issues with large datasets.
